boundaries.contract: `static void engine_list_cleanup(void)` — zero-argument cleanup callback registered with `engine_cleanup_add_last(Some(engine_list_cleanup))` at src/engine/eng_list.rs:161, only when `engine_list_add` first makes the list non-empty. Body loops on the module-static `ENGINE_LIST_HEAD: AtomicPtr<Engine>` (`load(Acquire)`) and calls `ENGINE_remove(head)` until the list empties — the same call the authority makes (`crypto/engine/eng_list.c:42-51`). No caller arguments; the sole path is OPENSSL_cleanup -> engine_cleanup_int -> cb(), and engine_cleanup_int is withheld (src/engine/eng_lib.rs:696-700), so it is unreachable at this identity. LIFETIME/CONCURRENCY CONCERN (why this is BLOCKED, not discharged): the `load` and the following `ENGINE_remove(head)` are separate operations. `ENGINE_remove` acquires the global engine write lock internally (src/engine/eng_list.rs:536-562), but the Acquire load is outside that critical section, so a concurrent `ENGINE_remove`/`engine_free_util` that frees `head` between the load and the lock would leave `ENGINE_remove` with a dangling `*mut Engine`. Today this is prevented only by the process-exit single-threaded ordering assumption, which is not proven here. Node lifetime is also not tied to the callback: each Engine is released by `engine_free_util` inside `ENGINE_remove`.
